analysis.title: AI quick pulse: NVDA 3QFY27 results - Strength in challenging times
key_insights: NVIDIA's 3QFY27 results beat consensus. Revenue was USD 115.8bn against USD 109.0bn consensus, and non-GAAP EPS was USD 2.68 against USD 2.48 consensus. The beat came from data center strength and solid profitability.

Data center revenue was USD 107.6bn, up 110% y/y. Hyperscaler revenue of USD 60.1bn grew 71% y/y against a 125% prior-year comparison. ACIE (AI Cloud, Industrial & Enterprise) revenue of USD 41.5bn grew 195% y/y as Vera Rubin shipments ramped to neocloud customers and frontier labs started building their own data centers.
Non-GAAP gross margin was 74.9% against 74.0% consensus and 73.6% a year ago. Non-GAAP operating margin was 67.2% against 65.8% consensus and 66.2% a year ago.
Guidance for the January 2027 quarter is USD 130.0bn plus or minus 3%, against USD 125.3bn consensus. It excludes any data center compute revenue from China.

Gross margin guidance of 71.0-72.0% brackets the 71.6% consensus. Management expects 4QFY27 to be the trough, with margins recovering to 72-73% in FY28. Operating margin guidance is slightly below expectations because of a 14-week quarter and transition costs.

Management raised its FY28 (January 2028) revenue growth outlook to about 75% y/y from 70%, citing higher demand and more supply availability. UBS expects earnings estimates to be revised up by mid- to high-single-digit percentages.

Following CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang's departure, management stressed the depth of its leadership bench. The board will consider internal and external CEO candidates. Management said memory and advanced-packaging capacity is secured and cited continued support from suppliers including TSMC.
Management said demand remains well above available supply. It expressed confidence that agentic AI and new model development can sustain demand into 2028.

Management signaled it sees no need to trade margins for market share despite competition from ASICs. The 4QFY27 trough reflects higher supply costs not passed on to existing customer purchase orders before new pricing takes effect.

NVIDIA will keep using customer financing but be more selective. Land, power and shell infrastructure are potential priorities, and third-party financing partners are expected to play a larger role. Neocloud guarantees are contingent on customers securing financing and infrastructure, which management said is not a new policy.

NVIDIA authorized a new USD 150bn buyback, bringing total capacity to USD 227bn. Management expects to use all of it by the end of 2028. It also plans to support suppliers with prepayments when needed.

UBS remains constructive on AI but notes this is the fourth year of the AI rally. It says incremental AI capex alone may not be enough, that cloud provider investment could be uneven, and that investors will focus more on monetization.

market_movers.rationale: The note is a results review with no rating or price target. UBS CIO expects estimates to rise mid- to high-single-digit percent after the beat and the raised FY28 growth outlook.

sector_views.rationale: UBS favors platform and application beneficiaries and enabling-layer infrastructure firms with pricing power. It stresses diversification across the Enabling, Intelligence and Application layers.
